title: The Year Everything Changed
theme: Five stops through Rome in the autumn of 1870 with Assunta Belli, a seamstress. In September the Italian army breaches the wall at Porta Pia and the Pope's Rome ends; in December the Tiber floods the city one last time before the walls go up.

companion.name: Assunta Belli
companion.brief: Twenty-nine, a seamstress working from a room near the river, taking in sewing for shops and households. Born in Rome. Sharp-eyed, careful about what she says out loud, since half her customers are on one side and half on the other. She watched the breach at Porta Pia from a rooftop and voted for nothing, being a woman, but has opinions. She knows nothing of the world after 1870.

presence.standing: at her work table by the window, cloth and thread spread in front of her, the narrow street outside behind
presence.gesture: pushes her needle into the cloth to keep it safe

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in Rome in 1870: ochre plaster, shuttered windows, laundry lines, unpaved squares, horse cabs, gas lamps, soldiers in the streets, the river running between low unwalled banks. Clothing of 1870: shawls, aprons, bowler and soft hats, uniforms. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Muted colour, not sepia.
style.avoid: no Tiber embankment walls (built after this), no Victor Emmanuel monument (1911), no motor vehicles, no electric light, no modern clothing, no text overlays

stops.title: Porta Pia
stops.brief: The gate and the broken stretch of wall beside it, hit by artillery on the twentieth of September until the papal troops raised a white flag.
mustCover: what happened here on the twentieth of September
how long the fighting lasted and who was hurt
what the city did that evening

stops.title: Piazza del Popolo
stops.brief: The great oval square where travellers arrive from the north, with the obelisk in the middle, now full of soldiers, newspapers and people arguing about the vote to come.
mustCover: the plebiscite and how the vote was taken
the obelisk and how old it is

stops.title: The Ghetto
stops.brief: The riverside quarter where Rome's Jews were locked in by night until two years ago: tall crowded houses, narrow lanes, a fish market, and the gates now gone.
mustCover: what the gates were and when they came down
what changes for the people here now

stops.title: The Tiber Banks
stops.brief: The river as it still is, without walls: mills and boats moored against the bank, steps down to the water, and the flood of December that put the streets under water again.
mustCover: how the river floods and how often
the mills and boats on the water
what is being proposed to stop it

stops.title: Piazza Colonna
stops.brief: The square on the Corso with the ancient column in it, newspaper offices and cafes around it, and crowds reading the proclamations posted up on the walls.
mustCover: how news travels in the city now
the column and what is carved on it
what people expect to happen next
